GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Purbalingga Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Purbalingga.
4. District is a part of the Regency Region led by a District Head.
5. District Head is the leader of the District who is under and responsible to the Regent through the Regional Secretary.
6. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers affairs in the Field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection Administration is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
12. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
14. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
15. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
16. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and children to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically and sexually.
17. Companion is a Social Worker who has professional competence in their field.
18. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems they face.
19. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into the family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children in accordance with the determined operational standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for regional apparatus, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the administration of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Integrated Service Center for Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of administration so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
23. District Level Complaint Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPPTK, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children located at the district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

I. GENERAL

Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, and neglect can occur in private, community or public domains.

Various causes of gender-based violence and violence against children include legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the role of media that does not support reporting on gender-based violence and violence against children, public services that are not yet optimal, poverty issues, misinterpretation of religious teachings, all of which cannot be separated from the strong patriarchal culture in society.

Therefore, victims of gender-based violence and violence against children need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. This Regional Regulation regulates the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, particularly with regard to prevention and services, protection mechanisms, community participation, guidance, funding, and supervision.

Article 16

Coordination and cooperation as referred to in Article 9 letter g include:
a. conducting coordination and cooperation in handling violence cases with UPPTK;
b. conducting coordination and cooperation with integrated service centers between regencies/cities; and
c. conducting coordination and cooperation with institutions providing services for victims of gender-based violence and children.

Article 23

1. In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other Regional Governments and/or other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Provincial Government or the Government includes consultation, coordination, advocacy, referral, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
3. Cooperation between the Regional Government and other Regional Governments includes coordination, advocacy, and referral.
4. Implementation of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by the principle of "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture, language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b
What is meant by the principle of "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c
What is meant by the principle of "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by the principle of "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, aligned, and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d
What is meant by the principle of "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e
What is meant by the principle of "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f
What is meant by the principle of "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making that can be taken into consideration, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter g
What is meant by the principle of "transparency" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.

Letter h
What is meant by the principle of "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, and police.

Letter i
What is meant by the principle of "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially, and economically.

Letter j
What is meant by the principle of "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Article 3

The Objectives of Protection Administration for Gender-Based Victims and Children are to:
a. prevent all forms of gender-based violence and violence against children, occurring within the scope of the household and/or community;
b. provide protection in the form of complaint services, health services, social rehabilitation services, legal assistance and enforcement services, and repatriation and social reintegration services; and
c. seek to increase community participation.

CHAPTER V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 24

The provision of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children is the joint obligation and responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. community;
c. family; and
d. parents.

CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

1. The Regent has the authority to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children.
2. The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus.

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION ADMINISTRATION

Part One

General

Article 4

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d
Neglect is: an act that results in the failure to meet the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of neglecting a person within the scope of their household; and/or an act that results in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e
Other violence constitutes any act caused by:
a. threat of violence, which includes any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom;
b. coercion, which includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. I. GENERAL

Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, and neglect can occur in private, community or public domains.

Various causes of gender-based violence and violence against children include legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the role of media that does not support reporting on gender-based violence and violence against children, public services that are not yet optimal, poverty issues, misinterpretation of religious teachings, all of which cannot be separated from the strong patriarchal culture in society.

Therefore, victims of gender-based violence and violence against children need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. This Regional Regulation regulates the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, particularly with regard to prevention and services, protection mechanisms, community participation, guidance, funding, and supervision.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection Administration is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
12. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
14. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
15. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
16. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and children to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically and sexually.
17. Companion is a Social Worker who has professional competence in their field.
18. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems they face.
19. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into the family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children in accordance with the determined operational standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for regional apparatus, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the administration of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Integrated Service Center for Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of administration so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
23. District Level Complaint Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPPTK, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children located at the district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by the principle of "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture, language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b
What is meant by the principle of "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c
What is meant by the principle of "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by the principle of "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, aligned, and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d
What is meant by the principle of "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e
What is meant by the principle of "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f
What is meant by the principle of "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making that can be taken into consideration, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter g
What is meant by the principle of "transparency" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.

Letter h
What is meant by the principle of "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, and police.

Letter i
What is meant by the principle of "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially, and economically.

Letter j
What is meant by the principle of "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

I. GENERAL

Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, and neglect can occur in private, community or public domains.

Various causes of gender-based violence and violence against children include legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the role of media that does not support reporting on gender-based violence and violence against children, public services that are not yet optimal, poverty issues, misinterpretation of religious teachings, all of which cannot be separated from the strong patriarchal culture in society.

Therefore, victims of gender-based violence and violence against children need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. This Regional Regulation regulates the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, particularly with regard to prevention and services, protection mechanisms, community participation, guidance, funding, and supervision.

Article 4

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d
Neglect is: an act that results in the failure to meet the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of neglecting a person within the scope of their household; and/or an act that results in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e
Other violence constitutes any act caused by:
a. threat of violence, which includes any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom;
b. coercion, which includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 10

Prevention Efforts as referred to in Article 9 letter a include:
a. organizing communication, information, and education about gender-based violence and children;
b. socializing laws and regulations related to gender-based violence and children.

Article 5

1. Protection Administration for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children is carried out by:
a. PPT PKBGA; and
b. UPPTK.
2. Principles in protection administration consist of:
a. fast, safe, and empathetic;
b. guarantee of confidentiality;
c. easily accessible; and free of charge.

Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
14. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
15. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
16. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and children to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically and sexually.
17. Companion is a Social Worker who has professional competence in their field.
18. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems they face.
19. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into the family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children in accordance with the determined operational standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for regional apparatus, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the administration of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Integrated Service Center for Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of administration so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
23. District Level Complaint Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPPTK, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children located at the district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Article 3

The Objectives of Protection Administration for Gender-Based Victims and Children are to:
a. prevent all forms of gender-based violence and violence against children, occurring within the scope of the household and/or community;
b. provide protection in the form of complaint services, health services, social rehabilitation services, legal assistance and enforcement services, and repatriation and social reintegration services; and
c. seek to increase community participation.

I. GENERAL

Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, and neglect can occur in private, community or public domains.

Various causes of gender-based violence and violence against children include legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the role of media that does not support reporting on gender-based violence and violence against children, public services that are not yet optimal, poverty issues, misinterpretation of religious teachings, all of which cannot be separated from the strong patriarchal culture in society.

Therefore, victims of gender-based violence and violence against children need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. This Regional Regulation regulates the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, particularly with regard to prevention and services, protection mechanisms, community participation, guidance, funding, and supervision.

Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by the principle of "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture, language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b
What is meant by the principle of "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c
What is meant by the principle of "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by the principle of "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, aligned, and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d
What is meant by the principle of "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e
What is meant by the principle of "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f
What is meant by the principle of "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making that can be taken into consideration, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter g
What is meant by the principle of "transparency" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.

Letter h
What is meant by the principle of "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, and police.

Letter i
What is meant by the principle of "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially, and economically.

Letter j
What is meant by the principle of "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Article 23

1. In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other Regional Governments and/or other institutions.

3. Cooperation between the Regional Government and other Regional Governments includes coordination, advocacy, and referral.

Article 4

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d
Neglect is: an act that results in the failure to meet the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of neglecting a person within the scope of their household; and/or an act that results in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e
Other violence constitutes any act caused by:
a. threat of violence, which includes any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom;
b. coercion, which includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

What is meant by the principle of "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c
What is meant by the principle of "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by the principle of "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, aligned, and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d
What is meant by the principle of "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e
What is meant by the principle of "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f
What is meant by the principle of "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making that can be taken into consideration, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter g
What is meant by the principle of "transparency" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.

Letter h
What is meant by the principle of "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, and police.

Letter i
What is meant by the principle of "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially, and economically.

Letter j
What is meant by the principle of "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Article 23

Article 4

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d
Neglect is: an act that results in the failure to meet the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of neglecting a person within the scope of their household; and/or an act that results in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e
Other violence constitutes any act caused by:
a. threat of violence, which includes any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom;
b. coercion, which includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Purbalingga Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Purbalingga.
4. District is a part of the Regency Region led by a District Head.
5. District Head is the leader of the District who is under and responsible to the Regent through the Regional Secretary.
6. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers affairs in the Field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection Administration is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
12. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
14. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
15. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
16. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and children to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically and sexually.
17. Companion is a Social Worker who has professional competence in their field.
18. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems they face.
19. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into the family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children in accordance with the determined operational standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for regional apparatus, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the administration of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Integrated Service Center for Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of administration so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
23. District Level Complaint Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPPTK, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children located at the district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

I. GENERAL

Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, and neglect can occur in private, community or public domains.

Various causes of gender-based violence and violence against children include legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the role of media that does not support reporting on gender-based violence and violence against children, public services that are not yet optimal, poverty issues, misinterpretation of religious teachings, all of which cannot be separated from the strong patriarchal culture in society.

Therefore, victims of gender-based violence and violence against children need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. This Regional Regulation regulates the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, particularly with regard to prevention and services, protection mechanisms, community participation, guidance, funding, and supervision.

Article 3

The Objectives of Protection Administration for Gender-Based Victims and Children are to:
a. prevent all forms of gender-based violence and violence against children, occurring within the scope of the household and/or community;
b. provide protection in the form of complaint services, health services, social rehabilitation services, legal assistance and enforcement services, and repatriation and social reintegration services; and
c. seek to increase community participation.

Article 23

1. In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other Regional Governments and/or other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Provincial Government or the Government includes consultation, coordination, advocacy, referral, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
3. Cooperation between the Regional Government and other Regional Governments includes coordination, advocacy, and referral.
4. Implementation of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

CONCERNING

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

BY THE GRACE OF ALMIGHTY GOD

REGENT OF PURBALINGGA,

Considering:

a. that every person has the right to be free from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity and has the right to obtain a sense of security, free from all forms of violence, discrimination and human rights violations; b. that victims of gender-based violence and children have increased so that victims must receive protection from violence and/or threats of violence inside and outside the household; c. that victims of violence need to be protected in their dignity and honor and guaranteed their right to life without discrimination and to provide legal certainty; d. that based on the considerations as referred to in letter a, letter b, and letter c, it is necessary to establish a Regional Regulation on the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children; In View of:

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Purbalingga Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Purbalingga.
4. District is a part of the Regency Region led by a District Head.
5. District Head is the leader of the District who is under and responsible to the Regent through the Regional Secretary.
6. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers affairs in the Field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection Administration is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
12. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
14. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
15. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
16. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and children to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically and sexually.
17. Companion is a Social Worker who has professional competence in their field.
18. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems they face.
19. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into the family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children in accordance with the determined operational standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for regional apparatus, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the administration of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Integrated Service Center for Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of administration so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
23. District Level Complaint Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPPTK, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children located at the district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Article 23

1. In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other Regional Governments and/or other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Provincial Government or the Government includes consultation, coordination, advocacy, referral, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
3. Cooperation between the Regional Government and other Regional Governments includes coordination, advocacy, and referral.
4. Implementation of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

I. GENERAL

Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, and neglect can occur in private, community or public domains.

Various causes of gender-based violence and violence against children include legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the role of media that does not support reporting on gender-based violence and violence against children, public services that are not yet optimal, poverty issues, misinterpretation of religious teachings, all of which cannot be separated from the strong patriarchal culture in society.

Therefore, victims of gender-based violence and violence against children need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. This Regional Regulation regulates the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, particularly with regard to prevention and services, protection mechanisms, community participation, guidance, funding, and supervision.

b. community;

d. parents.

Letter a
What is meant by the principle of "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture, language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

What is meant by the principle of "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c
What is meant by the principle of "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by the principle of "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, aligned, and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d
What is meant by the principle of "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e
What is meant by the principle of "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

Letter f
What is meant by the principle of "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making that can be taken into consideration, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter g
What is meant by the principle of "transparency" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.

Letter h
What is meant by the principle of "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, and police.

Letter i
What is meant by the principle of "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially, and economically.

Letter j
What is meant by the principle of "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Article 3

The Objectives of Protection Administration for Gender-Based Victims and Children are to:
a. prevent all forms of gender-based violence and violence against children, occurring within the scope of the household and/or community;
b. provide protection in the form of complaint services, health services, social rehabilitation services, legal assistance and enforcement services, and repatriation and social reintegration services; and
c. seek to increase community participation.

Article 4

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d
Neglect is: an act that results in the failure to meet the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of neglecting a person within the scope of their household; and/or an act that results in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e
Other violence constitutes any act caused by:
a. threat of violence, which includes any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom;
b. coercion, which includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 10

Prevention Efforts as referred to in Article 9 letter a include:
a. organizing communication, information, and education about gender-based violence and children;
b. socializing laws and regulations related to gender-based violence and children.

Article 3

The Objectives of Protection Administration for Gender-Based Victims and Children are to:
a. prevent all forms of gender-based violence and violence against children, occurring within the scope of the household and/or community;

Article 4

Letter a
What is meant by physical violence is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and/or causing death.

Letter b
Psychological violence is any act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering to a person.

Letter c
Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.

Letter d
Neglect is: an act that results in the failure to meet the needs of children properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, carried out by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;

an act of neglecting a person within the scope of their household; and/or an act that results in economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

Letter e
Other violence constitutes any act caused by:
a. threat of violence, which includes any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom;
b. coercion, which includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Purbalingga Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Purbalingga.
4. District is a part of the Regency Region led by a District Head.
5. District Head is the leader of the District who is under and responsible to the Regent through the Regional Secretary.
6. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers affairs in the Field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection Administration is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
12. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
14. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
15. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
16. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and children to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically and sexually.
17. Companion is a Social Worker who has professional competence in their field.
18. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems they face.
19. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into the family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children in accordance with the determined operational standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for regional apparatus, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the administration of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Integrated Service Center for Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of administration so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
23. District Level Complaint Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPPTK, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children located at the district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Article 23

1. In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other Regional Governments and/or other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Provincial Government or the Government includes consultation, coordination, advocacy, referral, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
3. Cooperation between the Regional Government and other Regional Governments includes coordination, advocacy, and referral.
4. Implementation of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by the principle of "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture, language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b
What is meant by the principle of "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c
What is meant by the principle of "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by the principle of "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, aligned, and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d
What is meant by the principle of "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e
What is meant by the principle of "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f
What is meant by the principle of "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making that can be taken into consideration, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter g
What is meant by the principle of "transparency" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.

Letter h
What is meant by the principle of "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, and police.

Letter i
What is meant by the principle of "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially, and economically.

Letter j
What is meant by the principle of "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

Article 3

The Objectives of Protection Administration for Gender-Based Victims and Children are to:
a. prevent all forms of gender-based violence and violence against children, occurring within the scope of the household and/or community;
b. provide protection in the form of complaint services, health services, social rehabilitation services, legal assistance and enforcement services, and repatriation and social reintegration services; and
c. seek to increase community participation.

Article 23

1. In providing protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government may cooperate with the Government, Provincial Government, other Regional Governments and/or other institutions.
2. Cooperation between the Regional Government and the Provincial Government or the Government includes consultation, coordination, advocacy, referral, monitoring, evaluation, and reporting.
3. Cooperation between the Regional Government and other Regional Governments includes coordination, advocacy, and referral.
4. Implementation of cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by the principle of "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinction of ethnicity, religion, race, class, sex, ethnicity, culture, language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter b
What is meant by the principle of "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies, and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.

Letter c
What is meant by the principle of "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by the principle of "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes harmonious, aligned, and balanced relations between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nation and state.

Letter d
What is meant by the principle of "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.

Letter e
What is meant by the principle of "child survival" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity.

What is meant by "child growth and development" is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to create and recreate.

Letter f
What is meant by the principle of "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making that can be taken into consideration, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.

Letter g
What is meant by the principle of "transparency" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among service providers.

Letter h
What is meant by the principle of "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, and police.

Letter i
What is meant by the principle of "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen victims, both physically, psychologically, socially, and economically.

Letter j
What is meant by the principle of "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure victims are in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychology of victims.

CHAPTER VII

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 28

1. The Regent has the authority to conduct guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and violence against children.
2. The authority as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be implemented by Regional Apparatus.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:
1. Region is Purbalingga Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Purbalingga.
4. District is a part of the Regency Region led by a District Head.
5. District Head is the leader of the District who is under and responsible to the Regent through the Regional Secretary.
6. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers affairs in the Field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
8. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural circumstances of society.
9. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
10. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
11. Protection Administration is a series of activities aimed at preventing violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
12. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
13. Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
14. Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who, because of their gender, experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
15. Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
16. Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and children to be more empowered, physically, psychologically, socially, economically and sexually.
17. Companion is a Social Worker who has professional competence in their field.
18. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems they face.
19. Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into the family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children in accordance with the determined operational standards.
21. Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for regional apparatus, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the administration of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
22. Integrated Service Center for Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of administration so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
23. District Level Complaint Service Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UPPTK, is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children located at the district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

I. GENERAL

Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are increasingly diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, and neglect can occur in private, community or public domains.

Various causes of gender-based violence and violence against children include legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the role of media that does not support reporting on gender-based violence and violence against children, public services that are not yet optimal, poverty issues, misinterpretation of religious teachings, all of which cannot be separated from the strong patriarchal culture in society.

Therefore, victims of gender-based violence and violence against children need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. This Regional Regulation regulates the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Violence Against Children, particularly with regard to prevention and services, protection mechanisms, community participation, guidance, funding, and supervision.

At the time this Regional Regulation comes into force, all implementing regulations related to the protection of victims of gender-based violence and violence against children are declared to remain in force as long as they have not been replaced and do not conflict with the provisions in this Regional Regulation.

Article 5

1. Protection Administration for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children is carried out by:
a. PPT PKBGA; and
b. UPPTK.
2. Principles in protection administration consist of:
a. fast, safe, and empathetic;
b. guarantee of confidentiality;
c. easily accessible; and free of charge.

Article 24

The provision of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children is the joint obligation and responsibility of:
a. regional government;
b. community;
c. family; and
d. parents.
